target_customer: Excel users in finance, operations and analysis who work with documents and unstructured data in spreadsheets
problem: Excel users cannot easily run AI over PDFs, web pages and text inside cells. Melder adds AI formulas such as GEN and EXTRACT, file uploads into cells, web scraping and a chat assistant, with citations.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription via Excel add-in (pricing not found)

founders.name: Ashwin Dharne
founders.background_notes: YC page: ex-Google security and cloud conversational AI.

founders.name: Philip Brewer
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as ex-Bain consultant.

competitors.name: FormulAI
competitors.what: Third party tool that turns text instructions into Excel formulas and explains formulas

technical_complexity.rationale: Excel custom functions that call language models, parse files and scrape pages were standard engineering in 2024; citation tracking adds some difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Microsoft was adding Copilot and an Excel Labs generative AI function, and other add-ins offered similar formulas, so a feature set like this was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search results show Microsoft Copilot formula features and an Excel Labs generative AI function in the Excel ecosystem, and a 2026 post discusses OpenAI work on Excel. No acquisition of Melder was found.

market_need_then: Excel is the default tool for analysis, and users often paste in documents and text they cannot process with formulas. LLMs made extraction and classification inside cells newly feasible in 2024.

branding.domain_note: Uses melder.io; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: not verified; company site could not be fetched from this environment

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing launched August 7, 2025 and a Microsoft Marketplace listing exist.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press or community evidence about the brand; the name is a generic word that also appears in other contexts.

outcome_analysis: Melder is an early stage Excel add-in from a two person New York team that joined YC in the Fall 2024 batch. It launched publicly on Product Hunt in August 2025. Public funding data is limited to an aggregator figure, and Microsoft's own AI features in Excel pose the main risk to the standalone add-in. There is no evidence yet of a strong outcome or a failure.
